commands.name: harness

commands.name: harness-resume

commands.name: harness-start

commands.name: harness-status

commands.name: harness-stop

commands.name: subagent-task-tree
commands.description: Execute a multi-task implementation plan as a chained subagent tree — you are the parent controller; you spawn one manager per task; each manager spawns a planner, a plan-auditor, one implementer per subtask, per-subtask auditors, and a final drift-auditor. (user)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify

commands.name: batch

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: built-in-browser

It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx

(user)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: anthropic-skills:deep-research

If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docs
commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: import-memory

A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: skill-creator
commands.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

## Problem Statement

A one-person online shop keeps its catalogue, stock movements and customer orders in three plain-text files (`catalog.txt`, `movements.txt`, `orders.txt`). The owner needs a tool that reads them and answers: what is on the shelves and what needs buying, what an order costs, and what can be shipped today — catching every mistake in the files with the file name and line number.

## Solution

A pure-stdlib Python (>= 3.9) package `stockroom`, installable with `pip install .`, that is both an importable library (`parse_catalog`, `parse_movements`, `parse_orders`, `stock_levels`, `price_order`, `ParseError`) and a `stockroom` console command with the subcommands `stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship` (the **shelves**) and `quote`, `fulfil`, `invoice`, `report` (the **orders**). The orders half builds on the shelves half. The full behaviour is specified in `## Original request` below, which is the top authority.

## User Stories

1. As the owner, I run `stockroom stock` / `stockroom low` to see what is on the shelves and how many of each low product to buy.
2. As the owner, I run `stockroom history SKU` to see every movement of a product with the running balance.
3. As the owner, I run `stockroom receive` / `stockroom ship` to append a movement safely; a movement that would break a rule leaves the file untouched.
4. As the owner, I run `stockroom quote ORDER` to see an order priced to the penny with volume discount, order discount and tax.
5. As the owner, I run `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` to ship what the shelves can cover without ever making a later movement go negative.
6. As the owner, I run `stockroom invoice ORDER` to bill only what has shipped, and `stockroom report` (text/csv/json) for an overview of every order.
7. As a scripter, I `import stockroom` and use the parse/stock/price functions directly, with `stockroom.ParseError` (a `ValueError` with `.line`) on bad input.
8. As the owner, any mistake in a file is reported on stderr with the file and line, exit 1, nothing on stdout; command-line and unreadable-file problems exit 2.

## Implementation Decisions

Decisions taken where the brief is silent (the brief wins on any conflict):

- **Layout**: `pyproject.toml` (setuptools, no runtime deps, `requires-python >= 3.9`), `src/stockroom/` package; console script `stockroom = stockroom.cli:main`; also `python -m stockroom`. Suggested modules: `parsing.py` (three parsers + `ParseError`), `shelves.py` (stock levels, status, low/buy, history, movement validation), `pricing.py` (`price_order`), `orders.py` (shipped-so-far, fulfil plan, status, invoice, report), `cli.py`. Products/movements/orders/quotes are frozen dataclasses. No 3.10+ syntax (no `match`, no `X | Y` annotations at runtime).
- **Text handling**: decode bytes as UTF-8 (strict; failure → exit 2), strip one leading U+FEFF, split lines on `\n` only and drop one trailing `\r` per line (never `str.splitlines()`). "Whitespace" for trimming, blank lines, comment detection and field separation means **space and tab only**. Digits are ASCII `[0-9]` only (use `re.ASCII` / explicit classes).
- **Field grammar**: SKU `^[A-Za-z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$` stored upper case. Price `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$` and `>= 0.01`. Reorder `^[0-9]+$`. Movement quantity `^[+-]?[0-9]+$`, non-zero (leading zeros allowed). Order id `^[Ss][Oo]-[0-9]+$` stored upper case, compared as the upper-cased string (`SO-7` != `SO-007`). Order line quantity `^[0-9]+$` and >= 1. Customer: any run of non-space/tab characters. A catalogue line has exactly 4 or 5 `|` fields; an empty tax field when 5 fields are given is a mistake.
- **Negative stock**: movements are stably sorted by date; the first movement (in that order) taking a SKU below zero is reported with **its own** file line number.
- **Error messages**: library `ParseError(message, line)` whose `str()` contains `line N`. CLI prints `stockroom: <file>: line N: <reason>` (or `stockroom: <reason>` when no file/line) to stderr.
- **Sorting**: "by SKU" = by the upper-case SKU string. Report: by order date, then by the numeric value of the order number, then the id string.
- **Money**: `Decimal` everywhere, `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `0.01`; all quote amounts quantized to 2 dp; render `-0.00` as `0.00`; discounts printed with `-` when non-zero. Order-discount allocation per step 4 of *Prices* (largest-remainder, earlier line wins ties).
- **Shipped so far** for an order line = minus the sum of negative quantities of that SKU over **all** movements (any date) whose note is exactly `order <ID upper>`, capped at the quantity ordered.
- **fulfil**: available on DATE = min(stock after all movements dated <= DATE, the minimum running stock after each later-dated movement), floored at 0; ship `min(owed, available)`; the new movements are appended at the end of the file (so they count after existing same-day movements). Lines with 0 shipped are still printed (`shipped 0`). Nothing to ship is not an error (exit 0, file untouched). Unknown order → exit 1; DATE before order date → exit 1; malformed DATE → exit 2.
- **invoice**: price an order made of the shipped quantities (lines with 0 omitted, original order) with `price_order`, so volume/order discounts apply to shipped quantities. Nothing shipped → exit 1.
- **receive/ship**: the new movement is validated by appending it to the parsed movements and re-running the full validation; refusal (exit 1) leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged. Bad DATE → exit 2 (mistyped date); bad quantity / unknown SKU / note containing `\n` or `\r` / negative stock → exit 1. Note is trimmed; an empty note means no note. The line written is `DATE SKU(upper) ±Q[ NOTE]`; if the existing file is non-empty and does not end in `\n`, a `\n` is written first. Wrong argument count → exit 2.
- **Command line**: hand-rolled parser (or argparse with care) — `--dir DIR` and `--dir=DIR` accepted anywhere; long options only, no abbreviations; `--json` only for stock/low/history/quote/invoice; `--format text|csv|json` only for report; any other `-`-led token is an unknown option (exit 2) **except** in receive/ship/fulfil where it is a positional argument. Checks run in the order: command line (2) → read files (2 unreadable, 1 mistake) → carry out (1 refused). `--dir` pointing at a missing folder → 2. Missing `catalog.txt` → 2; missing movements/orders → empty. Each command reads only the files listed in the brief.
- **Output**: stdout/stderr are written as UTF-8 regardless of locale. JSON via `json.dumps(obj, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` followed by a newline. CSV via the `csv` module with `\n` line endings. `BrokenPipeError` → silent exit 0 (redirect stdout to devnull before exit).

## Testing Decisions

- Tests use stdlib `unittest` (runnable with `python -m unittest` and pytest), under `tests/`. CLI tests call `stockroom.cli.main(argv)` with a temp `--dir` and capture stdout/stderr/exit code; one or two smoke tests run `python -m stockroom` as a subprocess (including the `| head -1` broken-pipe case).
- Every worked example in the brief is a test (the `stock` and `quote SO-1001` outputs exactly).
- Pricing is tested with hand-computed cases: volume tiers 9/10/49/50, the £500 threshold, half-up rounding at `0.005`, allocation remainders and the tie rule, mixed tax rates.
- Parse errors are tested per rule with the expected line number (including comment/blank lines counted, BOM, CRLF, lone `\r`, Unicode digits rejected).
- `pip install .` into a fresh venv provides `import stockroom` and the `stockroom` command (one integration test or CI step).

## Out of Scope

- Third-party packages, any GUI/web interface, editing `catalog.txt` or `orders.txt` from the tool, deleting/editing existing movements, currencies other than pounds, file locking/concurrent writers.

## Acceptance criteria

**Packaging & library**
- [ ] `pip install .` installs an importable `stockroom` package and a `stockroom` console command; stdlib only; works on Python 3.9+.
- [ ] `parse_catalog(text)` returns `dict` SKU → product with `.sku` (upper), `.name`, `.price` (`Decimal`), `.reorder` (`int`), `.tax` (`standard`/`reduced`/`zero`, default `standard`).
- [ ] `parse_movements(text, catalog)` returns movements in text order with `.date` (`datetime.date`), `.sku`, `.quantity` (`int`), `.note` (`str`, `""` when none).
- [ ] `parse_orders(text, catalog)` returns orders in text order with `.id`, `.date`, `.customer`, `.lines` (list of `(sku, quantity)` in written order).
- [ ] Any bad line raises `stockroom.ParseError` — a `ValueError` subclass with `.line` and `line N` in its message; line numbers count blank and comment lines from 1.
- [ ] All file rules of the brief are enforced: BOM ignored, LF/CRLF only line ends, blank/`#` lines skipped, SKU/name/price/reorder/tax grammar, duplicate SKU, real dates, catalogue SKUs, non-zero signed quantities, never-negative stock in date order (stable within a day, the offending line reported), order id grammar and uniqueness, `SKU*QTY` lines, SKU once per order, quantity >= 1.
- [ ] `stock_levels(catalog, movements)` gives every catalogue SKU's on-hand quantity (0 when never moved).
- [ ] `price_order(order, catalog)` follows *Prices* steps 1–6 exactly (half-up rounding, 5 %/10 % volume discounts, 3 % order discount at £500.00, largest-remainder allocation, per-line tax at 20/5/0 %), returning 2-dp `Decimal`s; discounts are <= 0.

**Shelves commands**
- [ ] `stock [--json]`: `SKU ONHAND STATUS NAME` by SKU with `out`/`low`/`ok`; reproduces the brief's example exactly.
- [ ] `low [--json]`: `SKU ONHAND REORDER BUY` for low/out products, `BUY = max(1, 2*reorder - onhand)`.
- [ ] `history SKU [--json]`: `DATE DELTA BALANCE[ NOTE]` in counting order; unknown SKU → exit 1.
- [ ] `receive` / `ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` append `DATE SKU ±Q[ NOTE]` (adding a missing final newline first, creating the file if needed) and print it; any rule violation is refused with the file left byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Orders commands**
- [ ] `quote ORDER [--json]` prints the header, per-line `SKU QTY UNIT GROSS DISCOUNT NET`, `subtotal`, `order discount`, `tax`, `total`; reproduces the brief's `SO-1001` example exactly; unknown order → exit 1.
- [ ] `fulfil ORDER DATE` ships `min(owed, available)` per line (owed from movements noted `order <ID>`; available capped by stock on DATE and the lowest later stock), appends `DATE SKU -N order <ID>` per shipped line, prints `SKU shipped N backordered M` lines and `status open|partial|complete`; DATE before the order date → exit 1.
- [ ] `invoice ORDER [--json]` prices the shipped quantities in the quote layout with `invoice ` before the header; nothing shipped → exit 1.
- [ ] `report [--format text|csv|json]`: one row per order sorted by date then order number; text `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`; csv header `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`; json objects with those keys, units as numbers, amounts as 2-dp strings.
- [ ] JSON shapes for stock/low/history/quote/invoice exactly as the brief lists (amounts strings, counts numbers, history `delta` a signed string).

**CLI behaviour**
- [ ] `--dir DIR` accepted anywhere; options spelled in full; receive/ship/fulfil take every non-`--dir` argument as typed.
- [ ] Each command reads only its files (shelves: catalog+movements; quote: catalog+orders; fulfil/invoice/report: all three); a mistake in an unread file is ignored.
- [ ] Exit 0 on success; exit 1 for data-file mistakes and refusals with a stderr message naming file and line and empty stdout; exit 2 for unreadable files (missing catalog, missing folder, non-UTF-8) and command-line errors (no/unknown command, wrong arg count, unknown option, bad option value, mistyped date); the command line is checked before files are read.
- [ ] A closed output pipe (`stockroom stock | head -1`) ends quietly with exit 0.
- [ ] A unittest suite covers every criterion above and passes on Python 3.9+.

- **Error messages**: library `ParseError(message, line)` whose `str()` contains `line N`. CLI prints `stockroom: <file>: line N: <reason>` (or `stockroom: <reason>` when no file/line) to stderr.
